use_when.text: Use a row of chips above a list to filter it, such as All, Wallets, Phones and Keys.
Use it to switch between report types, such as Lost and Found.
Set State to Active on every filter that is on. Start with All active.
Keep labels to one or two words.
Let the row scroll sideways on mobile when the chips do not fit.

dont_use_when.text: Do not use it to show an item’s status. Use Status Badge.
Do not use it for actions such as Submit or Save. Use Button.
Do not mix filter chips and buttons in the same row.
Do not recolour it outside the bound tokens.
Do not let a label run past two lines. Shorten it instead.

best_practice.text: Keep the chips in the same order on every screen, so people learn where each filter is.
Change the height with the density mode on the frame, not by hand.

variant_intent.intent: Use Default for a filter that is off.
Use Hover when the pointer is over it.
Set State to Active on every filter that is on. Start with All active.
Use Disabled when the filter is not available.

placement.text: Below Search Field, in a row of three Filter Chips, the first Active.
In a row of Filter Chips, the first Active.

a11y.text: Renders a native <button> with type="button" by default.
aria-pressed is true when State is Active and false otherwise.
State Disabled sets the native disabled attribute and drops onClick.
Build each chip as a button with aria-pressed="true" or "false", so screen readers announce whether the filter is on.
Group the row with a label, such as role="group" and aria-label="Filter by category".
Keep a visible focus indicator on keyboard focus (:focus-visible).
At 36 px the chip is under the 48 px touch target on Mobile. Extend its hit area to 48 px.
Label contrast is above 4.5:1 in every enabled state, including dark text on brand yellow (7.7:1 Light, 10.4:1 Dark).

gaps.detail: Filter Chip composes no other component and no story pairs it with a sibling component.
